types.embedding_query_text: CipherManuscript: A handwritten or printed document that contains encoded text using a cipher system. Also called encoded manuscript, ciphered document, cryptic codex. Examples: Borg cipher, Copiale cipher, Borg.lat.898, 408-page-long manuscript.

chosen_type.label: Manuscript
chosen_type.justification: A cipher manuscript is a handwritten document, which fits the broader Manuscript class.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: Text
candidates.comment: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".

candidates.label: PronounceableText
candidates.comment: PronounceableText is a data type for text that can be pronounced, often including phonetic or linguistic information. Also called phonetic text, spoken text. Examples: "schema.org" (pronounced "schema dot org"), "résumé" (pronounced "rez-oo-may"), a word with its IPA transcription.

types.embedding_query_text: Library: An institution that collects, preserves, and provides access to books, manuscripts, and other informational resources. Also called archive, repository, book collection. Examples: Vatican Library, Vatican library.

chosen_type.label: Library
chosen_type.justification: The Vatican Library is a concrete instance of the Library class.

candidates.label: Library
candidates.comment: A Library is a local business that provides access to books, media, and information resources. Also called public library, academic library, media center. Examples: New York Public Library, a university library, a local community library. Distinct from LibrarySystem, which is a collaborative network of libraries.

candidates.label: LibrarySystem
candidates.comment: A LibrarySystem is an organization representing a collaborative network or system among several libraries. Also called library consortium, library network, regional library system. Examples: a state library system, a university library consortium, a public library district. Distinct from Library, which is a single physical or organizational entity.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: Museum
candidates.comment: A Museum is a civic structure dedicated to preserving and exhibiting artifacts, art, or scientific specimens. Also called gallery, exhibition hall, cultural institution. Examples: The Louvre, Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, local art gallery. Distinct from Library, which primarily lends books and media.

candidates.label: ImageGallery
candidates.comment: An ImageGallery is a collection page web page type specifically designed to display a collection of images. Also called photo gallery, picture album, visual collection page. Examples: replacing a broken part with a new one, updating a document by replacing a paragraph, swapping out an old image for a new one, exchanging a product for a different model.

candidates.label: ReturnFeesEnumeration
candidates.comment: ReturnFeesEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different kinds of policies for product return fees. Also called return charge types, restocking fee types. Examples: FreeReturns, OriginalShippingFee, RestockingFee, ReturnShippingFee.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

candidates.label: PaymentMethodType
candidates.comment: PaymentMethodType is an enumeration for generic types of payment methods. Also called payment category, payment classification. Examples: CreditCard, DebitCard, BankTransfer, Cash. Distinct from PaymentMethod, which can be a specific instance or a broader concept.

candidates.label: DDxElement
candidates.comment: A DDxElement is an alternative, closely-related medical condition considered during differential diagnosis, along with the distinguishing signs. Also called differential diagnosis item, alternative diagnosis, rule-out condition. Examples: Considering "strep throat" as a DDxElement for a patient presenting with a sore throat and fever, alongside "common cold."

types.embedding_query_text: Language Examples: Arabic.

chosen_type.label: Language
chosen_type.justification: "Arabic" is a natural language, matching the Language class.

candidates.label: Language
candidates.comment: Language is an intangible representing natural languages such as Spanish or English, distinct from programming languages. Also called natural tongue, human language, spoken language. Examples: English, Spanish, Mandarin, Arabic. Distinct from ComputerLanguage, which refers to programming languages.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: QAPage
candidates.comment: A QAPage is a WebPage focused on a specific Question and its Answer(s), often found on question answering sites or FAQ documents. Also called FAQ page, question and answer page, knowledge base article. Examples: a Stack Overflow question page, a company's FAQ page, a support article addressing a common problem.

candidates.label: SpeakableSpecification
candidates.comment: A specification indicating, typically via CSS selectors or XPath, which sections of a document are particularly suitable for text-to-speech conversion. Also called speakable content definition, text-to-speech markup, voice-friendly section. Examples: a specification highlighting the main article text on a news page, a definition for a recipe's ingredients list.

candidates.label: Mosque
candidates.comment: A civic structure that is a place of worship for Muslims. Also called masjid, Islamic house of worship, Islamic center. Examples: "Blue Mosque", "Faisal Mosque", a local community mosque. Distinct from PlaceOfWorship, which is a broader category.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity Examples: 34 obscure symbols.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: "34 obscure symbols" denotes a measurable amount, fitting Quantity.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: TypeAndQuantityNode
candidates.comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.
